verevonRelevance: Quarry rejects or executes browser actions; recognising anti-bot walls as a first-class outcome (not an error) supports a human-takeover path and honest reporting.

name: Turn resilience: stall deadlines, paced retries and conversation-size caps
what: Turns have explicit deadlines (first token, mid-stream idle), classify provider overload and backend capacity deferral with a server-paced retry-after, and refuse at a conversation-size hard cap after garbage collection fails, telling the user to start a new conversation.

verevonRelevance: Agent turns in long rooms will hit context limits; a named hard cap with GC and an explicit "start fresh" path beats silent truncation.

name: Transcript write-ahead journal with checkpoints and rebuild
what: Conversation history is protected by a write-ahead journal and checkpoint root pointer: appends go to a journal, checkpoints are published atomically, corrupt or torn journals are discarded and rebuilt from the last checkpoint, and the turn fails closed if the checkpoint cannot be persisted.

verevonRelevance: Durable conversation state with fail-closed checkpoints is the integrity story behind "never lose a turn"; relevant to Session Core persistence.
notes: Where this journal runs (box host vs desktop host) is not confirmed; codes are in the desktop main-core registry.

name: Speculative attachment pre-upload and image pre-captioning while composing
what: The moment a file or image is staged in the composer, the desktop starts uploading it to the object store and, for images, asks the server to caption it in the background, so the agent turn can start with the attachment already prepared when the user presses send. Files that are never sent are released after a short grace period.

The pre-upload manager is keyed by staged path and scoped to agent plus session, supports hold and unhold during send, take() at send time, a 10 second release timer (expiry policy store-attachment-preupload-release) and a concurrency cap of 6. The pre-caption scheduler is debounced by 1 s, accepts png, jpeg, gif, webp and bmp up to 20 MiB, has a 150 s RPC deadline, backs off 10 minutes after a SKIPPED outcome and sends the draft text plus prior user messages as captioning context in StartGrokBotImagePrecaption. Outcome enum: CAPTIONED, ALREADY_CAPTIONED, NOT_NEEDED, SKIPPED, FAILED, SKIPPED_FOR_AGENT.

name: Composer editor engine: two surfaces, auto text direction, ARIA placeholder and macOS Emacs line motion
what: The message composer is a structured editor tuned for chat: formatting marks such as bold, italic, code and headings are switched off, leaving paragraphs, line breaks, links, mention chips and (in the main prompt) lists. It flips text direction per content, exposes its placeholder to screen readers, keeps the caret in view, groups undo steps quickly and supports Ctrl-A and Ctrl-E line motion on macOS. A second, lighter surface is used for skill-mention editing.
how: Tiptap 3 on ProseMirror (@tiptap/core, starter-kit, link, mention, placeholder, suggestion). Surfaces defined as prompt and skill-mention; starter-kit marks blockquote, bold, code, code block, heading, horizontal rule, italic, strike and underline are disabled; only the prompt surface gets lists, emoji suggestion and automatic direction, while caret scrolling and Emacs motion apply to both surfaces. Custom extensions sandComposerDirection (sets dir from content), sandAriaPlaceholder, sandScrollCaretIntoView, sandDocumentToken, sandMacEmacsLineMotion (Ctrl-A backward, Ctrl-E forward, Shift extends, bounded by hard breaks); undo group delay 100 ms; link marks do not auto-extend (inclusive false) and paste rules linkify only text that looks like a domain, scheme or localhost; mention nodes are atomic chips rendered through a node view.
verevonRelevance: Verevon v3 builds the composer in SolidJS; these details (RTL auto-direction, ARIA placeholder, caret scroll, paste linkify guard) are cheap parity items that Slack and Teams composers already have.
notes: Complements record 59 (mention menu and hotkeys); this record covers the editor internals.

name: Emoji shortcode completion with locale-aware emoji data
what: Typing a colon followed by letters in the composer offers matching emoji, with an emoji menu and picker available separately; completion is IME-safe and works off a local emoji catalogue that ships in many languages.
how: A ProseMirror plugin (sand-emoji-shortcode-completion) matches a trailing colon token of 1 to 50 characters inside a 60 character look-back window, builds a shortcode to emoji map from the emojibase catalogue, tracks candidate shortcodes and terminal inputs in plugin state, treats Tab as a special commit key and ignores composition (IME) events. Emoji names are translated through per-locale chunks (emoji-messages for af, ar, cs, el, ha, he, id, mr, sw, ta, te, tr, ur and others). The reaction picker most likely draws on the same catalogue (INF).
verevonRelevance: Reactions and shortcodes are table stakes in Space; the locale-chunked emoji catalogue shows how to keep bundle size down while supporting many languages.

name: Link previews with hover cards and a byte-budgeted cache
what: Links in messages unfurl into cards and hover previews with title, description, favicon and image; unwatched previews live in a bounded cache that sheds large images first, then all images, then favicons, and previews are fetched and cached per account.
how: Renderer cache sand-link-preview-eviction with an unwatched-preview budget of 8 MiB, split into 7 MiB for images and 1 MiB for metadata, a fixed per-entry overhead of 256; eviction first drops image data larger than 64 KiB, then any image, then favicons, while entries with live watchers are never evicted; image decode runs under a task boundary with a budget of 8 decodes and 8 Mi characters. Desktop main process fetches metadata through getLinkMetadata with a cache directory per account scope (link-preview-cache); the call also accepts an optional beforeHover argument whose semantics were not confirmed.
verevonRelevance: Link unfurling in Space should be server-side per tenant (Quarry or Application Plane) with an explicit cache budget and per-account partitioning so previews never cross tenants.
notes: Fetching is described in the next record (SSRF guard).

name: SSRF-safe link unfurling in the desktop main process
what: Link metadata is fetched only over HTTPS to public hosts, with redirects re-validated and the connection pinned to the resolved address, so a crafted link in a chat cannot make the app probe a private network.
how: URL validation rejects non-HTTPS, credentials in the URL, custom ports, URLs over 2048 characters, single-label and localhost names and any IP in a block list covering 0.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 100.64/10, 127/8, 169.254/16, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, test and documentation nets, multicast, and IPv6 loopback, ULA, link-local and transition ranges. Hostnames are resolved with a 3 s deadline, every returned address must be public, and the request connects to the resolved address with the original Host header and SNI. Maximum 5 redirects (301, 302, 303, 307, 308), each re-validated; 8 s request deadline; identity encoding; response byte limit raises LinkPreviewTooLargeError.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon surface that fetches user-supplied URLs (link previews, agent browsing outside Quarry) must apply the same resolve-then-pin, block-list and redirect re-validation, and should live in the Ingestion plane rather than in clients.
notes: Quality 4: thorough, but it runs on each desktop client rather than on a shared service, which duplicates the guard per device.

name: Virtualized transcript with a shared virtualizer, positioned rows and reaction-shift animation
what: Long conversations are virtualized: only rows near the viewport are in the DOM, rows are positioned absolutely, off-screen state is observed, and when a reaction row appears below a message the rows above slide smoothly instead of jumping.

verevonRelevance: Verevon v3 Space rooms with long agent transcripts need virtualization with stable anchors; epoch-keyed layout caches and FLIP for late-arriving rows are worth copying in SolidJS.

name: Activity vocabulary: 20 activity kinds with rotating friendly phrases
what: What a Bot is doing is shown with short human phrases chosen by activity kind: thinking, working, searching or reading the web, reading or drafting a file, on its own or your computer, running commands, organizing files, waiting on a command, generating a photo or video, coding, messaging, connecting an app, browsing and checking usage. Thinking and working have several variants picked by a stable fraction so the label does not flicker.
how: A map in the renderer from activity kind to message id (thinking has 3 variants, working 5, the rest one each); a selector picks a variant by index = floor(fraction x variants), clamped, where the fraction is supplied by the caller (presumably a stable per-turn value, INF, so the label does not flicker); kinds mirror the tool activity in GrokBotAgentLiveState.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should map Model Plane run states and tool calls to one small, localized activity vocabulary with deterministic phrase choice, shared by sidebar, room header and notifications.
notes: Extends record 12 (live states) and 114 (copy style) with the concrete kind list.

name: Feedback on a Bot answer with four reasons, plus a separate product feedback path
what: Each answer can be rated with thumbs; a thumbs-down opens a short form with reason chips (not what I asked, inaccurate, low quality, too slow) and a free comment. Product feedback goes through a Send Feedback menu item and dialog with an option to ask for a reply from support and to attach the conversation id; only the Bot owner can rate, and abuse is rate limited.
how: Chunk view with category ids not_what_i_asked, inaccurate, low_quality, too_slow and strings Good result and Bad result; transcript kind entry:feedback; application menu Help item emits open-feedback; feedback dialog (sand-feedback-dialog, 460 px) with two checkboxes (include the current conversation id, and request a reply from the support team) and a typed error map: invalid-feedback, not-signed-in, rate-limited (several reports in a short time), subscription-required (a paid plan is needed to send feedback) and unavailable.
evidence: dist/renderer/assets/index.eager-app-CY939ORZ.js lingui-id s7XoNw "Only the owner can send feed..."
dist/renderer/assets/index.eager-app-CY939ORZ.js lingui-id GzMvLf "I would like a response from..."
verevonRelevance: Result-level feedback with a small fixed reason set gives Verevon a cheap quality signal for agent turns that can feed the cost and evaluation views in the Model Plane.
notes: Where reports are stored and who reads them is server-side and unknown. Extends record 61 (reactions and feedback votes).

name: Editable draft cards with revision highlights and an unconfirmed-send state
what: A message the Bot drafts for email, Slack or a meeting chat appears as a card with From, To, Cc, Subject and Message fields you can edit, send or discard. When the Bot revises a draft, the changed body text and changed fields are highlighted for a few seconds, and a send whose result is uncertain is marked unconfirmed with advice to check the destination.
how: Chunks view render email, Slack and meeting cards (sand-email-composer and siblings). A revision hook compares the current draft entry with a baseline entry earlier in the transcript chain, produces a highlight with body diff operations and a changedFields list, keeps it in a phase map (shown then fading) with a 10 second timer, and skips animation under reduced motion; fields in the list get a Changed in this revision label. Card states are Ready to send, Sending, Sent, Discarded, Unconfirmed and Message not delivered; an approval-mode switcher (always allow, needs approval, disable drafts) and an inline offer to save a custom allow rule share the card.
verevonRelevance: Draft cards with visible revision diffs are the right hand-off pattern for outbound agent messages in Space, where a human approves or edits before anything leaves the tenant.
notes: Complements records 37 and 64; this record covers the revision highlight and the card states. The baseline lookup walks earlier transcript entries, so a revised draft is a new entry linked to the earlier one.

name: Team Bots gated by a multiplayer flag, team membership and the durable server harness
what: Shared Team Bots only appear for people who are in a team and in the multiplayer rollout, and only agents that run on the durable server harness can be published to a team. A deep link that tries to create a Team Bot without that access shows an explanatory alert.
how: Feature gate grok_bot_multiplayer plus a team requirement (Y_ = multiplayer enabled and has team); helper functions test harness equals temporal, visibility equals team and not a group before enabling publish and management actions; viewer-is-owner or can-manage decides who edits; the deep-link router rejects create-team-bot with the reason team-bots-unavailable and logs a tagged warning; sidebar markers for team Bots (avatar chip, title chip, avatar start) depend on the same flag.
verevonRelevance: Sharing an agent with a team depends on an agent runtime that has durable identity; Verevon should make the same dependency explicit (agent bindings need a durable owner-plane identity before they can be shared in a Space).
notes: Rollout flags are runtime state and were not observed. Related to records 3 and 92.

name: In-app deep-link router: Bot, task thread and create-Team-Bot routes
what: Deep links open a specific Bot, a specific task thread inside a Bot, or the Team Bot creation flow, and are rejected with an alert if the account cannot use Team Bots.
how: Renderer function validates a parsed deep link (isDeepLink), handles route agent (select Bot), a task link with agent and id (open the task thread) and route create-team-bot (launch creation through the launcher with a busy and superseded guard and a per-account feature-gate check); anything else falls through to a generic handler. OAuth return handling is covered by record 110.
verevonRelevance: Space links should address room, thread and agent task consistently so notifications, emails and agent messages can deep-link into the exact context.
notes: Scheme registration and OAuth relays are in record 110.

name: Native application menu with update-state item, unread-only filter and Help
what: The desktop menu bar offers Settings, a View menu with Reload, an unread-only Bots filter toggle and full screen, developer tools only in dev builds, and a Help menu with the Help Center and Send Feedback; on macOS an About item and, outside macOS, a Check for updates or Restart to update item appear depending on update state.
how: Menu template in main-app.cjs: accelerator CmdOrCtrl+, for Settings, CmdOrCtrl+R for reload, a checkbox item bound to isUnreadFilterChecked that emits an unread-filter event to the renderer, devtools gated by canUseDevTools and prefixed DEV, F11 or the native full-screen role, Help Center URL docs.x.ai/grok-bot, Send Feedback emitting open-feedback, and an update item computed from the update service state (hidden, check enabled or disabled, restart with version) that is reinstalled only when the item changes.
verevonRelevance: A Verevon desktop wrapper should expose the same few native affordances (settings, unread filter, feedback, update state) without adding menu sprawl.
notes: The unread-only filter being a native menu toggle is an unusual placement.

name: Platform-specific window chrome with zoom-aware control inset
what: The app draws its own header and adapts to each OS: Windows uses native caption buttons through a title bar overlay with a light or dark tone, Linux gets custom minimize, maximize or restore and close buttons, and macOS keeps traffic lights; page zoom does not break the inset.
how: Renderer component sand-window-controls returns null on macOS, a hidden placeholder on Windows that sets CSS variables --sand-window-controls-inset (140 px divided by --sand-zoom-factor) and --sand-window-controls-block, and calls setTitleBarOverlayTone through a window-commands bridge; Linux renders buttons with Minimize window, Maximize window or Restore window labels and hides them in full screen; failures go to a diagnostic reporter.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships an Electron or Tauri shell, a custom header must reserve control space with zoom compensation; this is the pattern.
notes: Behaviour of the title bar overlay API itself is Electron.

name: Dock and taskbar unread badge projected from the roster with sequence guards
what: The app icon badge shows the number of unread messages across Bots, skipping Bots hidden from the sidebar or with notifications off, and ignoring stale roster snapshots so the number never moves backwards.
how: A projector sums max(floor(unreadCount or 1), 1) for agents that have unread, are not hidden and have notifications enabled, then calls setBadgeCount only when the projected total changes; snapshots are accepted only when the epoch matches and the sequence is newer; for server-harness agents the count follows a server-side verdict when one is available (an agent missing from the verdict is not counted; agents are counted while the verdict is unknown or awaited), with a re-read owed when the roster changes during a read; failures are reported as a dock-badge edge failure.
verevonRelevance: Badge counts must respect mute and hidden state and be monotonic under out-of-order snapshots; Space should derive the badge from the same unread projection as the sidebar.
notes: Complements record 62 (read state) and record 75 (notification routing).

name: Top-layer overlay management with the Popover API
what: Menus, dialogs and toasts are mounted into a dedicated overlay layer that is promoted to the browser top layer, and is re-shown when a new dialog opens so overlays always stack correctly above other top-layer content.
how: The renderer defines a marker attribute data-sand-overlay-layer, looks up that element (falling back to body) as the portal container, and calls hidePopover then showPopover on it to move it to the top of the top-layer stack; reduced-motion state is read through matchMedia in the same module.
verevonRelevance: A single popover-based overlay root removes z-index wars in SolidJS and keeps native dialogs, menus and toasts consistent; worth adopting for Space.
notes: Medium confidence on intent (inferred from the re-show trick); behaviour not run.

name: Hold-to-reveal sidebar shortcut hints
what: Holding the Command key (macOS) or Control key (Windows and Linux) for half a second reveals numbered shortcuts on sidebar Bots; pressing any other modifier or leaving the window hides them again.
how: An idle-timer helper sand-sidebar-shortcut-hold (500 ms) armed on keydown of the chosen modifier, cancelled by any other modifier chord, by keyup when the modifier is no longer held, and by the page becoming hidden; hints render as a command-glyph or control-glyph plus the digit; sidebar items are drag-and-drop zones with ids of the form sand-sidebar-{kind}:{id} and Team Bot markers.
verevonRelevance: Hold-to-reveal shortcut hints teach power-user navigation without permanent clutter; cheap to add to a Space channel and agent sidebar.
notes: The shortcut itself (focus sidebar Bot N) is in record 103.

name: Screen-reader live-region announcer with polite and assertive channels
what: Status changes that are not visible focus changes are announced to assistive technology through two hidden regions: a polite status region and an assertive alert region, so repeated identical messages are still spoken.
how: Component renders div role status (aria-atomic) with class sand-announce-polite and div role alert with class sand-announce-assertive, each wrapping a span keyed by a tick counter so identical text re-announces; the store resets both channels on unmount.
verevonRelevance: Agent activity changes constantly; Space needs an announcer layer so screen reader users hear completions and approvals without every row being a live region.
notes: This is one of very few explicit accessibility features found; there was no high-contrast or forced-colors handling in the renderer.

name: Accessible pane navigation: push and pop transitions, inert outgoing pane and focus hand-off
what: Moving between panes (for example new chat to a Bot) animates with a wipe or crossfade, but the outgoing pane is made inert and hidden from assistive technology, focus moves to the new pane or its first heading, and the animation is skipped for users who prefer reduced motion.
how: Hook and component in chunk wipe-navigation: navigate(direction push or pop, landing target) stores a landing focus target, renders the outgoing pane with aria-hidden and inert and an onAnimationEnd cleanup, and variants incoming and outgoing push, pop and crossfade; focus logic uses a temporary tabindex -1, a MutationObserver that waits for headings to appear and for inert or aria-hidden to clear, and skips focus stealing when something else already has focus; a reduced-motion check disables the transition.
verevonRelevance: Verevon v3 should adopt the focus-handoff rules (inert outgoing view, heading focus, reduced-motion bypass) for every animated route change, including Space switching.
notes: Quality 5 because it handles the usually missed cases: inert subtree, late-rendered headings and focus already moved by the user.

name: Right-hand details pane with close linger, focus hand-off and resize handle
what: A details pane on the right shows Bot settings, routine detail, computer preview and async tasks; it can be toggled by shortcut, resized by dragging a labelled separator, and optionally shows a task thread beside the main chat when the window is wide enough.
how: The info pane keeps itself mounted for 300 ms after close (agents-info-pane-close-linger) so exit animation completes, becomes inert while closing, and moves focus to the first enabled button once the pane is interactive; the resize handle is a role separator with an aria-orientation and the label Resize details; settings Open Threads Beside the Main Chat controls whether a task thread docks beside the chat; commands toggle details and toggle Bot settings.
evidence: dist/renderer/assets/index.eager-app-CY939ORZ.js lingui-id oQJQPF "Open Threads Beside the Main..."
verevonRelevance: Space needs a context pane (members, agents, tasks, files) that adapts to width; the linger plus inert plus focus rules are the accessible way to build it.
notes: Complements record 14 (async tasks) and record 116 (computer view).

name: Bot hover card: what it is awaiting, drafting or last said
what: Hovering a Bot in the sidebar shows a card with its avatar, status marker and a one-line preview chosen by priority: what it is waiting on from you, a pending draft, its last message, or a no-messages-yet text.
how: Component sand-agent-hover-card selects the preview from awaiting reason first (with a localized reason), then a draft label plus first line, then the last-entry preview, then the empty text; the avatar marker shows working or unread state.
verevonRelevance: Space member and agent hover cards should prioritize blocking state (awaiting approval) over last message, so humans see what needs them first.
notes: Preview priority is read from the code path order; exact styling not examined.

name: Stale-transcript notice and scoped error boundaries
what: When a Bot runs on its own computer and the transcript may be out of date, the chat shows a banner saying saved messages are being shown; each screen sits behind its own error boundary that resets when you switch Bots, so one failing view does not take down the app.
how: The chat screen renders a notice component when isStaleTranscriptNoticeDue is true and the agent harness is not the durable server harness; error boundaries named chat_screen reset on currentAgentId and report to telemetry with a boundary tag; strings for section-level errors and a render-error reload hint exist.
evidence: dist/renderer/assets/index.eager-app-CY939ORZ.js lingui-id lXHsrk "This section hit an unexpect..."
verevonRelevance: Space should state when it is rendering a cached or degraded view of a room instead of silently showing old data, and isolate failures per pane.
notes: Trigger condition of isStaleTranscriptNoticeDue is computed elsewhere; only the display rule was read.

name: Computer lifecycle progress as an accessible step list with a progress bar
what: While a Bot computer is created, updated, reset or recovered, the user sees an ordered list of steps with done, active and pending states and a progress bar, with copy such as Creating the computer, Moving files over, Backing up your data and Starting desktop.
how: Components sand-agent-computer-step-list (ordered list with aria-label) and sand-agent-computer-step-row (aria-current step on the active row, state icon check, spinner or circle, a visually hidden state text) plus sand-agent-computer-progress-bar with a value clamped to 0 to 1; steps derive from lifecycle kind, stage and migration phases, with a heartbeat component for long operations.
verevonRelevance: Any long agent-environment operation in Space (sandbox provisioning, browser grant, reset) should show named steps with an accessible progress representation instead of a spinner.
notes: Complements records 15 to 17.

name: Mention and reference menu scoping by conversation type
what: The @ menu offers different candidates depending on where you are: in a group chat only its members, in a 1:1 chat all other Bots and groups that include this Bot, with Team Bots you have not added hidden; the composer can also reference pull requests, MCP items and skills.
how: Composer context supplies getMentionMembers, getMentionPeople, getNoMentionMembers, prReferenceCandidates, referenceableSkills and mcpReferenceItems; a scoping function returns the group member ids for a group, otherwise every agent except the current one, groups containing the current Bot, and filters Team Bots not added when hidesUnaddedTeamBots is on.
verevonRelevance: Space mention candidates must be scoped by room membership and by ACL so an agent or person never appears for someone who could not address them.
notes: Complements record 59.

name: Bot creation with client-generated identity, optional kickstart introduction and language
what: A new Bot can introduce itself and open the conversation in the user language right after creation, or be created silently; creation is idempotent because the client generates the Bot id and the server must confirm that same id.
how: CreateGrokBotAgentRequest carries agent_id (the client nonce), harness, kickstart_requested, introduction_suppressed, language, purpose, origin, create_intent (FRESH or REGISTER_EXISTING_LOCAL), create_caller (ROOM_MEMBERS, ENSURE_SERVER_BACKED, MINT, BACKFILL, PRODUCT_CREATE) and created_automatically; the desktop creates the durable agent with a 45 s timeout and treats a response whose id or harness does not match as data loss; suppressing the introduction is the default unless a kickstart was requested. A failed introduction becomes a transcript event.
verevonRelevance: Space agent bindings should be created with client-supplied idempotency keys and an optional first-contact message, so retries never duplicate agents and new agents greet in the right language.
notes: Complements records 1, 2 and 6.

name: Provider-aware link cards for external documents
what: Links the Bot shares to external documents are shown as cards with the right icon and a document kind (page, document, spreadsheet, presentation, design or file) based on the provider, such as Notion, Google Sheets, Google Slides, Figma, Miro, Canva, Confluence, Slack canvas, GitHub, OneDrive, SharePoint, Box and Dropbox.
how: Two lookup tables in the renderer: provider to brand (microsoft-365, figma, jira, github, slack, box, dropbox, canva, hex and more) and provider to kind (page, spreadsheet, presentation, design, file); an untitled fallback title per kind (Untitled page, document, spreadsheet, presentation, design, file) and a hostname fallback; markdown files are parsed in a web worker that reports parsing, ready and failed states in chunks.
verevonRelevance: Space should recognize externally hosted documents (SharePoint, Google, Figma) as typed artifacts with provider icons and respect that Space access never widens the source ACL.
notes: It shows the product treats external documents as first-class references rather than owning all artifacts.

name: Voice call client state machine with call island, recoverable-close policy and reconnect
what: A voice call with a Bot has explicit phases (connecting, live, reconnecting, ending, failed), a mute state, an activity indicator and a duration timer. A call control follows you to other Bots while the call runs, and dropped connections are retried unless the user hung up, the remote side ended normally or the microphone failed.
how: Renderer call controller with a state shape {phase, agentId, callId, startedAtMs, isMuted, activity, turns, nudges, failure, fault}; static helpers isCallerOnTheLine, isCallUnderway and canHangUp; controlPresentation hides the control when you are viewing the Bot you are talking to (a popover is shown there), shows an active control when you navigate elsewhere and offers no call in group chats; closeIsRecoverable treats hang_up, a normal remote close and microphone_unavailable or microphone_prompt_unanswered as final; timers include a 1 s duration tick, a 1.5 s hang-up presence deadline and a live-presence retry policy of up to 5 attempts between 250 ms and 2 s; chat header carries a data-voice-call-island-shown attribute; a constant named rating-only next to the call constants hints at a post-call rating mode (INF, not confirmed).
verevonRelevance: If Space adds agent voice, it needs the same explicit call lifecycle (reconnect policy, mic failure handling, navigation-persistent call control) rather than a modal that dies on navigation.
notes: Extends records 50 and 127 (voice persona and per-Bot voice). Realtime audio transport is covered by the runtime facet.

name: Client restore orchestration with a 30 second stuck detector and staged failure telemetry
what: On launch the app restores sign-in, first-run state, local-tool permission, machines, plan access, terms acceptance and saved accounts as one lifecycle; if restore does not finish in 30 seconds the app records a stuck outcome with the stage it reached, and a failure carries a coded error with a client-owned retry command.
how: A composition root builds members auth, firstRun, onboardingRun, localToolPermission, machines, sandAccess, grokBotTerms and savedAccounts and starts them as a single lifecycle; a restore watchdog (sand-client-restore-stuck, timeoutMs 30000) ships a client_restore event with outcome failed or stuck, the last marked stage, a generation number, elapsed milliseconds and an error class; the failure code client/restore-failed names boundary client and retry owner client with command restore.
verevonRelevance: Verevon v3 should treat startup as a named, staged lifecycle with a watchdog and a coded retry path so a hung session restore is observable instead of a blank window.
notes: Related to the coded error registry in record 120.

name: First-run gate: onboarding decided from sign-in, saved flag, roster size and computer creation
what: Whether a user sees onboarding is computed rather than assumed: signed-in state, a saved onboarding-seen flag, whether the account already has Bots and whether a new computer is still being created. Existing accounts with Bots are not shown onboarding on a new device, onboarding can be skipped, restarted from settings or forced, and a slow or unanswerable check fails open.
how: A gate state machine (checking, gate-probing-box, gate-awaiting-box-creation, gate-unanswerable, gate-landed, onboarding, shell) with a probe-patience timer that emits box-silent, an agent count probe, device-onboarded memory and commands connect, reconnect, signed-out, signed-in, account-switched, forceOnboarding, restartOnboarding (clears the seen flag), skipOnboarding (checks sign-in first), completeOnboarding and markOnboardingSeen (persists the flag and confirms the main Bot); isAccountOnboarded consults seen flag and roster under a deadline and returns veto-seen, veto-roster or fail-open-deadline; steps and completion are reported to telemetry.
verevonRelevance: Space onboarding should be a derived decision (membership, existing agents, provisioning state) with fail-open behaviour, so returning users on a new device are never forced back through setup.
notes: Complements record 113 (onboarding content). The gate also reports a sign-in gate outcome to telemetry.
